steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Effect on Structure: Serialisation required cliffhangers at chapter ends. Each instalment needed a hook to make readers buy the next. This creates episodic, suspenseful pacing. | Moral Purpose: Victorian novels often had explicit moral messages. Dickens used fiction to campaign for social reform. Literature was seen as a way to educate and improve society. | Victorian Values: Novels promoted hard work, charity, self-improvement, and Christian morality. Characters who ignore these values face consequences. | AO2 Conventions Strategy: When analysing a 19th century novel, AO2 (language, form, structure) typically carries 33% of marks. The highest-achieving responses don't just identify conventions — they explain why the writer chose them and what effects they create. Examiners reward analysis
